lede: Tuesday is the heaviest day on the civic calendar: a newly seated Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would write new landscaping and historic-review standards into the Land Use Code — a real vote on rules that affect nearly every property in town. The Housing Authority meets the same day to hash out a primary-residency policy for dependents in multi-custodial households, and Wednesday the BOCC holds a special meeting with no agenda posted yet, which is worth watching. Thursday, Planning and Zoning digs into the Carhenge redevelopment and SMART's board votes on two gondola structural-analysis contracts.

notable.stake: Second-reading vote on wildfire code changing land-use and landscaping rules townwide.
New primary-residency policy for dependents of multi-custodial households up for adoption.
Public review of Carhenge redevelopment subdivision and concept plans on Town-owned land.
Board votes on two gondola structural-analysis contracts critical to the gondola's future.
Public hearing on KOTO's Live at the Drive liquor permit — residents may comment.
